rfi.description: Marine Le Pen has promised to lead France towards a national “rebirth” as she closed the National Rally’s congress in Orléans on Sunday, combining an optimistic vision of the country’s future with hardline pledges on immigration, security and sovereignty.

rfi.title: High turnout in Serbia as student movement takes on Vucic at the polls
rfi.description: Serbian voters queued in unusually long lines on Sunday as a student-led movement sought to turn almost two years of protests into an election breakthrough, mounting the biggest challenge to Aleksandar Vucic’s rule in more than a decade.

rfi.title: France reports 1,314 arrests after protests as police defend security operation
rfi.description: Police arrested 1,314 people and 53 officers were injured during Saturday’s protests across France, the interior ministry said on Sunday, as authorities defended a reinforced security operation aimed at keeping marches safe and protecting shops.

rfi.title: Suspect in deadly Paris suburb shooting moved to psychiatric unit
rfi.description: A man suspected of carrying out a gun attack that killed one person and wounded five in the Paris suburbs has been transferred from police custody to a psychiatric unit for observation, French anti-terror prosecutors said on Sunday.

rfi.title: A life lived in music: Nadia Boulanger, the musicians' mentor
rfi.description: By the time she died, 47 years ago this week, Nadia Boulanger had taught some of the 20th century’s greatest musicians. Generations of composers, conductors, performers and arrangers passed through her apartment in Paris. More than a midwife to male genius, she was an exceptional talent in her own right.

rfi.title: France and Britain test NATO readiness with major airborne exercise in Germany
rfi.description: French paratroopers have joined British forces in a major military exercise in Germany, testing their ability to deploy together to defend Nato territory against an enemy equipped with drones and electronic warfare capabilities.

rfi.title: 'The major risk remains a human-directed attack', cyber threat expert warns RFI
rfi.description: Artificial intelligence is changing the pace of cybercrime, helping attackers hunt for security weaknesses, break into computer systems and steal valuable information. For the specialists trying to stop them, the challenge is to keep up. Cyber threat expert François Deruty told RFI this means finding ways to turn the same technology to their advantage.

rfi.title: ‘We want to stop being afraid’: thousands join anti-RN demonstration in Orléans
rfi.description: Thousands of people marched peacefully through Orléans on Saturday to protest against the far-right National Rally as the party held its congress a few kilometres away, with demonstrators calling for solidarity and voicing their concerns about 2027.

rfi.title: 'Go green and go thirsty': Guinea’s plastic ban clashes with need for safe water
rfi.description: Plastic water sachets are an essential way to provide people in Guinea with safe and affordable drinking water. But their use clashes with the government’s objective of outlawing single-use plastics. Until a solution can be found, authorities have been forced to lift a ban, less than three weeks after implementing it.

rfi.title: Paris march ends in clashes after largely peaceful protests across France
rfi.description: Clashes broke out at the end of a Paris protest on Saturday after a largely peaceful march that drew 110,000 people, according to police, as fresh demonstrations took place across France.

rfi.title: Young Israeli voters lean right, as election puts Netanyahu to the test
rfi.description: Young Israelis preparing to vote in parliamentary elections on Tuesday are leaning further to the right than their elders, with some drawn to the far right and its focus on security. In Rehovot, a city whose results tend to mirror the national vote, RFI met a generation shaped by the attacks of 7 October, 2023 and three years of war.

rfi.title: Azerbaijan hijab ban exposes strain in ‘brotherly’ ties with Turkey
rfi.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, a staunch advocate of Muslim rights, has been notably silent on Azerbaijan’s recent hijab ban in schools. For years, Erdogan and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev have shared a close alliance, but the ban is putting the Turkish president in a tight spot.

rfi.title: Deadly shooting west of Paris ‘clearly terrorist’ attack, interior minister says
rfi.description: One person was killed and four others were wounded, including a 12-year-old girl, when shots were fired from a car in two suburbs west of Paris on Friday. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said the shooting was “clearly a terrorist crime” and “a racist, probably Islamophobic attack”.

rfi.title: France mobilises 70,000 police and gendarmes for Saturday protests
rfi.description: France will deploy some 70,000 police officers and gendarmes nationwide during a fresh round of protests this weekend, Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday, as President Emmanuel Macron met with student organisations at the Élysée Palace for the first time since the high school protests started more than a month ago.

rfi.title: ‘Too arrogant, too sure of itself’ France confronts its legacy in Africa
rfi.description: Fifteen years after France promised a new relationship with Africa, Paris is still struggling to reconcile its rejection of colonial-era interference with its desire to retain influence on the continent. RFI Africa specialist Christophe Boisbouvier argues in a new book that France can still build a partnership of equals – based on respect rather than arrogance or domination.

france24fr.description: A la Une de la presse, ce lundi 26 octobre, la réélection, au Brésil, du président Lula pour un quatrième mandat. Les réactions, en France, au lancement officiel de la campagne de Marine Le Pen, la candidate du RN, pour la présidentielle de 2027. Le Rassemblement national, accusé par la gauche d’avoir nourri le racisme de l’auteur présumé de l’attentat qui a tué une personne et blessé plusieurs autres, à Trappes, en banlieue parisienne, vendredi dernier.

france24fr.title: Le Real Madrid remporte le Clasico face au FC Barcelone grâce à Kylian Mbappé
france24fr.description: Le Real Madrid a battu le FC Barcelone en Liga (2-1) grâce à un doublé de Kylian Mbappé et revient à 3 points de son adversaire du soir au classement.

france24fr.title: À gauche comme à droite, les dirigeants d'Amérique latine saluent la victoire de Lula au Brésil
france24fr.description: De nombreux dirigeants d'Amérique latine ont réagi dimanche soir à la réélection de Lula à la tête du Brésil. Les dirigeants de gauche ont salué une victoire pour la démocratie, tandis que les chefs d'État de droite appellent à la coopération avec le Brésil.

france24fr.title: 🔴 Présidentielle au Brésil : Flavio Bolsonaro dit qu'il va "demander l'annulation des élections"
Brésil : Lula réélu président, Flavio Bolsonaro va demander "l'annulation des élections"
france24fr.description: Contre toute attente, le chef de l'État sortant du Brésil Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva a vaincu son opposant Flavio Bolsonaro dimanche soir lors du deuxième tour de l'élection présidentielle, avec plus de 51,79 % des voix. Refusant de reconnaître les résultats, Flavio Bolsonaro a déclaré qu'il allait demander "l'annulation des élections".

RD Congo : la proposition de loi fixant les conditions d’organisation du référendum adoptée
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, l’Assemblée nationale adopte à nouveau la proposition de loi fixant les conditions d’organisation du référendum. Un texte qui encadre notamment la possibilité de réviser la Constitution ou d’en adopter une nouvelle. L’opposition dénonce une manœuvre qui pourrait ouvrir la voie à un troisième mandat de Félix Tshisekedi.

france24fr.title: Éthiopie : que veut vraiment Abiy Ahmed pour son pays ?
france24fr.description:
L'Éthiopie, un géant africain à l'histoire millénaire, mais un pays profondément divisé.
 
Quatre ans après l'accord de Pretoria, les tensions persistent et les fractures politiques restent entières. Pourquoi est-il si difficile de construire un projet commun dans ce pays aux multiples peuples, langues et traditions ? france24fr.title: Serbie : Aleksandar Vucic concède sa défaite aux législatives anticipées
france24fr.description: Figure dominante de la vie politique en Serbie depuis 14 ans, le dirigeant nationaliste Aleksandar Vucic a reconnu sa défaite aux législatives anticipées dimanche, admettant rapidement dans la soirée que le mouvement étudiant avait remporté la victoire, après avoir mené des manifestations pendant deux ans.

france24fr.title: Marine Le Pen lance sa campagne pour l'élection présidentielle à Orléans
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen a officiellement lancé sa campagne pour l’élection présidentielle française ce dimanche 25 octobre avec un meeting à Orléans.

france24fr.title: Pour les électeurs de Marine Le Pen, "c’est faux de dire que le RN incite à la haine"
france24fr.description: Marine Le Pen tenait son premier meeting de campagne dimanche à Orléans, deux jours après l’attaque terroriste raciste qui a fait un mort et cinq blessés à Trappes. En dépit d’un discours qui stigmatise les étrangers et les musulmans, les électeurs du parti d’extrême droite refusent d’y voir un lien avec le drame de vendredi.

france24fr.title: La prix Nobel Maria Corina Machado de retour au Venezuela après près d'un an d'exil
france24fr.description: "Je suis là. Avec vous tous", a ​écrit sur les réseaux sociaux Maria Corina Machado, à son retour dimanche au Venezuela. ‌La lauréate du prix Nobel de la ⁠paix et cheffe ⁠de file ​de l'opposition vénézuélienne vient de passer près d'un an dans la clandestinité à l'étranger.

france24fr.title: Midterms 2026 : Obama fait campagne pour les démocrates et épingle Trump
france24fr.description: Lors d'un meeting dans l'Ohio, l'ancien président américain Barack Obama a accusé le président actuel Donald Trump d'avoir déclenché une guerre "inutile" en Iran.

france24fr.title: France :  Paris aux couleurs de la NFL
france24fr.description:
Le Stade de France est encore une fois entré dans l'Histoire en accueillant, dimanche 25 octobre, le premier match de saison régulière de #NFL, le championnat des États-Unis de football américain.
 
Pour cette rencontre inédite entre les #Saints et les #Steelers, les fans sont venus en nombre de la Nouvelle-Orléans et de Pittsburgh, mais aussi de France et d'autres pays européens. Nos journalistes @taise.parente et @stbslam sont allées à leur rencontre.

france24fr.title: Marine Le Pen appelle ses militants à être "au rendez-vous de l’histoire"
france24fr.description: Dans son discours au congrès du Rassemblement national, Marine Le Pen a réaffirmé la place de la "priorité nationale" dans son projet politique et appelé ses militants à être "au rendez-vous de l’histoire". La candidate d’extrême droite s’est également réclamée de Jeanne d’Arc, évoquant sa figure face à une menace étrangère. Retour sur les messages et les références de ce discours avec Elena Volochine, envoyée spéciale sur place, et Flore Simon, chroniqueuse politique.

france24fr.title: Au congrès du RN, les militants confiants avant le discours de Le Pen
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes sont réunies pour la deuxième journée du congrès du Rassemblement national, avant le discours de Marine Le Pen prévu ce dimanche après-midi. Les militants affichent leur optimisme, confortés par des sondages qui placent leur candidate en tête après les manifestations du 17 octobre. france24fr.title: Hommage à Aubervilliers à Pengo Bossio Wangi, la garde à vue du tireur levée
france24fr.description: Un hommage à Pengo Bossio Wangi, jeune espoir du MMA, a eu lieu ce dimanche après-midi dans le centre d’Aubervilliers. La garde à vue du tireur présumé a été levée pour motif psychiatrique. Que sait-on de cette décision et de la suite des investigations ? V. Lerouge et E. Pelletier font le point sur l’enquête.

nzz.description: Die komplizierte Struktur mit zehn Regionalgenossenschaften bremst den Detailhändler im Kampf gegen Coop und die Discounter. Nun schlägt die Migros-Spitze grundlegende Veränderungen vor.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Audi-Chef Döllner taucht an einer Wahlveranstaltung von Trump auf. Dabei sollte er Autos verkaufen, nicht Haltung zeigen
nzz.description: Der Autohersteller Audi braucht Absatz und Wettbewerbsfähigkeit – auch unter einem erratischen Präsidenten wie Donald Trump. Audi muss weit über dessen Abgang hinaus planen.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Angstzustände und geistige Lähmung: Immer mehr junge Chinesen verlieren den Glauben an eine bessere Zukunft
nzz.description: Job-Angst und gesellschaftlicher Druck führen dazu, dass sich immer mehr junge Menschen aus dem Wirtschaftsalltag verabschieden. Für die ehrgeizigen Pläne der chinesischen Regierung zur Modernisierung des Landes ist das nicht gut.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Frankreich brennt: «Respekt gegenüber Autoritätspersonen ist nicht mehr vorhanden»
nzz.description: Junge Menschen im Westen seien narzisstisch, sagt der Politologe Jérôme Fourquet. Dadurch stelle sich die Frage nach dem Fortbestand der Gesellschaft – nicht nur in Frankreich. Der Regierung Macron wirft Fourquet vor, das eigene Land nicht zu kennen.

nzz.title: Drohnen über dem Stromnetz: Sollen Energieversorger selbst zur Waffe greifen dürfen?
nzz.description: Drohnen bedrohen Kraftwerke und Stromnetze. Die Betreiber verstärken den Schutz, dürfen aber selbst kaum eingreifen. Nun wächst der Druck auf den Bund.

nzz.title: Ariel, die neue Bachelorette, stellt sich dumm, verkauft ihre Privatsphäre – und wird dafür gut bezahlt. Sie sagt: «Dieser Deal ist nicht schlecht, oder?»
nzz.description: Begegnung mit einer, die ihr Innerstes brutal nach aussen kehrt.

nzz.title: «Eine einzige Sicherheitslücke kann eine Kettenreaktion auslösen»: Die Versicherer rüsten sich gegen KI-gestützte Cyberattacken
nzz.description: Die jüngst entdeckten PHP-Sicherheitslücken sind ein Warnsignal für die Versicherungsbranche. Treffen Cyberangriffe unzählige Unternehmen gleichzeitig, können die finanziellen Schäden wie bei Erdbeben und Pandemien gewaltig sein.

nzz.title: Bund vergibt Auftrag von 60 Millionen ohne Ausschreibung an die SBB
nzz.description: Gemäss dem Bundesamt für Rüstung kommt nur eine Bahn infrage. In einigen betroffenen Bereichen spielt jedoch der Wettbewerb.

nzz.title: «Wenn man etwas liebt, möchte man nicht, dass es aufhört»: Stan Wawrinka lädt zum letzten Tanz in Basel

nzz.title: Die EU will SpaceX aus strategischen Gründen ausbremsen – die USA reagieren mit Drohungen
nzz.description: Bald schon verbinden sich normale Handys direkt mit Satelliten. Um technologisch unabhängiger zu werden, will die EU einen Teil der Frequenzen reservieren. Vier Telekom-Firmen steigen in den Ring.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Machtkampf im Orbit – warum der Weltraum strategisch und sicherheitspolitisch so relevant ist
nzz.description: Mehr denn je ist unsere digitalisierte Gesellschaft auf die Nutzung des Weltraums angewiesen. Derzeit umkreisen rund 15 000 Satelliten die Erde. Ihre Zahl wächst rasant, und ihr Zweck übersteigt das Zivile. So hat der Rüstungswettlauf über unseren Köpfen längst begonnen.

nzz.title: Putin übt «Vergeltung» indem er Schulen, Spitäler und Supermärkte bombardiert. Doch das wird ihm nichts nützen
nzz.description: Die Angriffe der Russen richteten sich zuletzt häufig auf zivile Ziele. Die Ukrainer würden das überstehen, weil sie die Nachkommen jenes «neuen Typs Mensch» seien, der von den Kommunisten gezüchtet wurde, schreibt der Schriftsteller Sergei Gerasimow aus Charkiw.

nzz.title: Auf der Flucht vor Wohnungsnot und hohen Preisen in der Stadt: Das sind die attraktivsten Agglomerationen und Vororte in der Schweiz
nzz.description: Die Zuwanderung und mangelnde Bautätigkeit machen Wohnraum in den Städten knapp und teuer. Viele Familien suchen ihr Glück in Vororten oder noch weiter draussen. Ein neuer Gemeindevergleich kürt die besten Alternativen zu den Zentren. Teil 1 der Immobilien-Serie «Raus aus der Stadt».

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Hellere Städte für kühlere Sommer
nzz.description: Die Schweiz leidet zunehmend unter Sommertemperaturen, welche das als normal empfundene Mass sprengen. Ideen zur Kühlung sind gefragt, vor allem in den grossen Städten. Eine einfache und auch real wirksame Massnahme wäre eine flächige Aufhellung der Dächer.

nzz.title: VW ID. Polo: Mit dem E-Kleinwagen findet Volkswagen zu alter Stärke zurück
nzz.description: Der neue Stromer überzeugt bei ersten Testfahrten. Er punktet mit viel Platz und gutem Fahrwerk. Doch auf einem Gebiet hat er noch Nachholbedarf.

observador.description: Bolsonaro não reconhece a reviravolta histórica de Lula devido ao prolongamento da votação. No Congresso, é a direita que lidera. Que governação vai ter o Brasil? Uma conversa com José Carlos Duarte.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale
undark.description: Welcome to the last installment of Entanglements, at least for the foreseeable future. In this final episode, hosts Brooke Borel and Anna Rothschild are joined by Undark editor-in-chief Tom Zeller Jr. to talk about the show’s successes, failures, and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

phys-org.title: Lumina simulation brings the early universe to life on a record-breaking scale
phys-org.description: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and Nancy Roman Space Telescope are revealing the universe's earliest chapters in detail. To help astronomers understand what they are seeing, researchers at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian have developed "Lumina," one of the largest and most detailed simulations ever created of the early universe.

phys-org.title: Experienced teachers are quitting or reducing their hours—they're struggling to cope
phys-org.description: Teacher shortages are affecting school systems in countries across the world. Governments have responded with initiatives to attract graduates into teaching. While much attention has focused on increasing supply, far less attention has been paid to why experienced teachers decide to leave, despite the high costs of turnover in recruitment, training and lost continuity.

phys-org.title: Assessment tool helps schools look at students holistically
phys-org.description: Researchers in the Neag School of Education are bringing a whole child screening assessment to a company that provides schools with a connected set of solutions that turn every student signal into timely, equitable, coordinated and measurable tools to track and manage supports.

phys-org.title: Australian coral reefs face risk of collapse within 50 years without drastic action, global assessment finds
phys-org.description: Every shallow-water coral reef ecosystem in Australia faces an extremely high risk of collapse by 2075, driven largely by projected ocean warming, according to a global assessment.

phys-org.title: Supercurrent enables the reading of quantum information without destroying it
phys-org.description: One of the fundamental challenges of quantum computing is obtaining information from a quantum bit, or qubit. Unlike a conventional bit, which can be read repeatedly without altering its content, direct measurement of a quantum system typically causes the state to collapse before it can be determined. In other words, reading the information modifies it.

phys-org.title: Crows make decisions twice as fast as humans and monkeys
phys-org.description: University of Tübingen researchers have shown that crows, when confronted with a visual choice, make a decision twice as fast as humans and monkeys. In the experiment, two carrion crows took just 235 milliseconds on average to identify the direction in which a dot pattern was moving and to indicate their choice—while maintaining a high degree of accuracy.

phys-org.title: Storms batter Europe, hitting power supplies, flights and phones
phys-org.description: Storms battered northern Europe on Sunday, cutting power to more than 150,000 homes, forcing the cancellation of hundreds of flights and silencing phone networks.

phys-org.title: Monarchs report their locations via… cellphone?
phys-org.description: Who knew a monarch butterfly could borrow a cellphone to check in with friendly people he met on his journey? That is essentially what happens now that new technology has reduced the weight of a radio-pulse tag to less than half a gram (0.02 ounces).

phys-org.title: Milky Way's disk grew 'upside down,' with younger stars forming in ever-thinner layers
phys-org.description: The Milky Way is home to hundreds of billions of stars arranged in a glorious spiral pattern. But beyond the obvious spiral, our galaxy has other physical characteristics. It's divided into a galactic bulge, a galactic disk and a galactic halo.

phys-org.title: How screening tools measure disadvantage may leave rural communities overlooked for public support
phys-org.description: Whether a community is prioritized for public support can depend on how its needs are measured, according to new research from the University of New Hampshire. The study found significant differences in how government screening tools identify communities, particularly in rural areas where those differences could affect access to funding.

phys-org.title: Patterns of polar vortices discovered in lead-free superlattices on silicon
phys-org.description: A team at HZB has, for the first time, reported polar vortices in (BaTiO₃/SrTiO₃)₁₀ superlattices on silicon. These results expand the range of materials and substrates on which polar topological textures can occur and open up new options for incorporating complex ferroelectric states into silicon-based technologies.

phys-org.title: Protecting children from harm isn't enough—welfare systems must support healing through quality mental health care
phys-org.description: In Quebec and across Canada, people working in child welfare do remarkable work to protect children and youth from maltreatment and to support families facing complex challenges.

phys-org.title: A few seconds of loading time can push online learners off track
phys-org.description: An online lesson takes an extra second to load. The wait may seem trivial, but in a study examining  large learning platforms, these brief pauses were linked to unfinished assignments, lower scores and less time spent on the site.

phys-org.title: Microorganisms show promise for reducing emissions from manure
phys-org.description: Dairy farmers sometimes use additives in their cattle housing to reduce emissions from slurry. Emissions of substances such as ammonia occur when urine and feces mix on the floor of the housing. At the same time, dairy farmers want to increase the fertilizing value of the manure when it is applied to agricultural land.

phys-org.title: Southern Africa's first known stenciled rock art found hiding in plain sight
phys-org.description: Southern Africa has one of the most detailed and elaborate bodies of rock art anywhere in the world, from herds of running antelope to dancing men and humanoid beings with wings, hooves and horns. All are painted with fine brushstrokes or fingers. One thing this art lacks is stencils.

phys-org.title: Global underground CO₂ storage hit record 43.6 million metric tons in 2024 alone
phys-org.description: The most comprehensive record yet of carbon dioxide stored underground through geological carbon dioxide storage has been published today, revealing that 43.6 million metric tons were sequestered in 2024 alone—a new annual record—and that 421.7 million metric tons have now been stored in the past three decades.

phys-org.title: Sea cucumber–inspired gel could help heal damaged tissue in humans
phys-org.description: Inspired by the ability of sea cucumbers to change the stiffness of their bodies, University of Waterloo researchers have developed a gel that could one day help repair damaged tendons and other soft tissues without leaving permanent material behind.

phys-org.title: Who should have a say in which species are saved? The California condor offers lessons for a global biodiversity treaty
phys-org.description: In 1987, biologists captured the last free-flying condor to transfer it to captivity, and the largest flying North American bird species was officially declared extinct in the wild. Today, after decades of coordinated efforts and millions of dollars spent on captive breeding and reintroduction efforts, more than 300 condors have been restored to their natural environment.

While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not ac

proj-syn.title: Who Pays the Fiscal Watchdogs?
proj-syn.description: Civil-society oversight is the cheapest insurance in sovereign finance, because it enables independent scrutiny long before a default. But given that a borrowing government will never volunteer to fund the people who audit it, global decision-makers must do so using agreements for stolen-asset recovery and sovereign-debt treatments.

proj-syn.title: How to Help Left-Behind Regions
proj-syn.description: Pouring public investment into poorer towns and cities might be politically beneficial, but the economic returns of indiscriminate largesse would be limited. A better approach would concentrate investment in areas with the potential to become high-productivity hubs, such as large peripheral cities.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: A Competitive Europe Must Be Climate-Resilient
proj-syn.description: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years. The consequences for Europe’s competitiveness and economic security are clear—and so is the appropriate response.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Prepare for the Worst
proj-syn.description: Those seeking to weaken the EU’s supranational foundations are already preparing their radical schemes, like the “new deal for Europe” that Germany's Alternative für Deutschland recently presented in the European Parliament. The pro-EU camp must be prepared with new political strategies and institutional arrangements.

proj-syn.title: Nature Can’t Wait
proj-syn.description: Although the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine are spurring governments to increase spending on defense and focus more on economic growth, it would be a mistake to postpone investments designed to protect nature. In fact, meeting internationally agreed targets could add up to $450 billion to annual global GDP by 2050.

proj-syn.title: Argentina’s Economic Chainsaw Massacre
proj-syn.description: Argentine President Javier Milei may currently be a lynchpin in US President Donald Trump’s geoeconomic vision for Latin America; but he could soon become its weak link. With elections coming next year, he has achieved an economic recovery and relative price stability by driving millions of his people into destitution.

proj-syn.title: Which AI Myth Will We Embrace?
proj-syn.description: The mythos—or foundational stories—that we tell ourselves will determine our fate in the age of AI. As industry leaders regale us with utopian visions of benevolent digital gods delivering scientific breakthroughs and expanding our technological horizons, our best defense against hubris is a counternarrative of social cooperation.

proj-syn.title: No More Superpowers
proj-syn.description: Although the United States remains very powerful and Russia still commands enormous conventional and nuclear capabilities, each country’s global status has come to be defined by failure and constraint. If anything, both may belong to the same broad grouping of middle powers that includes the likes of Canada, Brazil, and India.

proj-syn.title: What’s Driving Persistent Inflation?
proj-syn.description: In their preoccupation with high public debt, rising bond yields, and dizzying AI valuations, investors have seemingly forgotten the supply shocks shaping the underlying inflation outlook. But anyone worried about debt and yields must reckon with the disruptions created in the name of protecting domestic markets.

proj-syn.title: Building the Economy Africa Needs
proj-syn.description: Africa cannot control global geopolitics, let alone prevent external shocks. But it can manage its exposure, especially by building an integrated continental market, investing in higher-value-added production, and pushing for reform of the global credit-rating agencies.

proj-syn.title: Science Without Scientists?
proj-syn.description: Now that autonomous systems are capable of generating their own hypotheses, designing experiments, and writing up the results, the scientific community must adapt. For scientific knowledge to retain its standing, its sources must be trusted and answerable to the public.

proj-syn.title: When Smart Cities Turn Menacing
proj-syn.description: Uganda has embraced digital-surveillance tools in the name of improving public safety and combating terrorism, a pattern that is repeating itself across several African countries. But governments are increasingly using these technologies for political control, rather than for national security.

proj-syn.title: Brazil Cannot Afford Bolsonaro’s Spending Cuts
proj-syn.description: If he wins the October 25 runoff, far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro plans to slash public spending by as much as 1.5% of GDP. These cuts could push Brazil into recession, hurt workers and small businesses, and drain tax revenue—all without solving the country’s debt problem.

proj-syn.title: A Generational Reckoning on the Streets of Paris
proj-syn.description: As their schools deteriorate and the planet grows hotter, many young people in France do not have hope for a decent future. The recent protests may foreshadow a broader conflict between older generations who wield political power and younger people who must live in the world they leave behind.

proj-syn.title: The Algorithm Driving French Student Protests
proj-syn.description: One of the main drivers of the student protests in France is the opposition to Parcoursup, the country’s university-admissions platform, which is widely denounced as opaque and unfair. While such automated decision-making systems do not create educational inequalities, they can exacerbate them.

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI Drives A Varied Lineup Of Large Financings
crunchbase.description: It was another interesting week for AI-related startup funding, with a number of large rounds and quirky companies. The largest financings went to Tenstorrent, a developer of AI processors and systems, and AI lab Flapping Airplanes. The quirkiest round, meanwhile, was undoubtedly a $200 million financing for Warhound, which wants to breed elite military dogs. A number of big rounds in areas including biotech, space tech and physical AI rounded out the list.

crunchbase.title: Protecting Trade Secrets In The Age Of AI
crunchbase.description: AI agents create new trade secret risks by allowing employees to access expertise or inadvertently expose proprietary information through personal devices. In this guest commentary, Seth Kugler, a partner at Grellas Shah LLP, warns companies that they should adopt strict AI policies, restrict data access on unmanaged devices, update confidentiality agreements, and act immediately when misuse is suspected.

crunchbase.title: The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It.
crunchbase.description: In this guest article from Airrived co-founder and CEO Anurag Gurtu, he contends that Anthropic’s rapid revenue growth does not justify its proposed $2 trillion IPO valuation, given enormous infrastructure commitments, safety concerns, customer concentration and competition from cheaper open-weight models, saying instead that lasting enterprise AI value will come from proprietary data, reliable deployment and measurable customer outcomes rather than expensive models alone.

crunchbase.title: Acquirers Are Snapping Up Boom-Era Startups That Haven’t Raised Funding In Years
crunchbase.description: A number of companies whose names might feature on a playlist of 2021 boom-era unicorns have sold to acquirers in recent months, including one-time highfliers like Airtable, Headspace and Miro. In many cases, companies are selling at valuations which, while not puny, are still far below their former peaks.

crunchbase.title: Your Next Customer Might Be An Agent. Here’s How To Build Your Brand For Both Humans And AI.
crunchbase.description: As AI agents increasingly recommend and purchase products, brands must appeal to both machines and humans by documenting their voice, creating clear product descriptions and checking how AI summarizes their messaging. Guest author Toby Coulthard suggests that startups should build these practices in from the outset, preserving human appeal while measuring success through conversions and revenue rather than content volume.

crunchbase.title: When A Startup Sells, Its Employees’ Equity Plans Can Change Overnight
crunchbase.description: Startup acquisitions can reshape employees’ finances and careers, with individual outcomes depending on a variety of conditions. Guest author Ron Honig, co-CEO and managing partner of From-Honig Family Office, suggests that before making major life changes, employees should clarify their award rights, when proceeds will become available, and what their after-tax payout can realistically support.

crunchbase.title: ‘Weird And Maybe Uninvestable’: How Reach Capital Spots Its Venture Winners
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase News spoke with James Kim, partner at Reach Capital, about how Reach’s education roots inform its broader strategy, what it saw in AI detection company GPTZero, and why some of its best investments initially divided its own team. We also discussed how ownership stakes and secondary transactions have shaped the firm’s approach to returning capital.

crunchbase.title: How To Build A Billion-Dollar Company Without Venture Capital
crunchbase.description: Founders can build billion-dollar businesses without venture capital by prioritizing customer revenue, pricing for quality, hiring exceptional talent and automating processes to scale efficiently, argues Nacho De Marco, who draws on his experience bootstrapping BairesDev, to emphasize financial discipline and a lasting commitment to solving customer problems as the foundations of sustainable growth.
